title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop as a rectangle with the following lines: the first line from zero, zero to zero point zero two zero eight, zero; the second line from zero point zero two zero eight, zero to zero point zero two zero eight, zero point zero two zero eight; the third line from zero point zero two zero eight, zero point zero two zero eight to zero, zero point zero two zero eight; and the fourth line from zero, zero point zero two zero eight to zero, zero. Inside the first rectangle, draw a smaller rectangle for the second loop with the following lines: the first line from zero point zero zero one three, zero point zero zero one three to zero point zero one nine five, zero point zero zero one three; the second line from zero point zero one nine five, zero point zero zero one three to zero point zero one nine five, zero point zero one nine five; the third line from zero point zero one nine five, zero point zero one nine five to zero point zero zero one three, zero point zero one nine five; and the fourth line from zero point zero zero one three, zero point zero one nine five to zero point zero zero one three, zero point zero zero one three. Apply a scaling factor of zero point zero two zero eight to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translate it using the translation vector zero, zero, and zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by zero point seven five units, without extruding in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from the extruded two-dimensional sketch. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object are length zero point zero two zero eight three three three three three three three three three units, width zero point zero two zero eight three three three three three three three three three units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer and inner loops of the sketch
outer_loop = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.0208, 0.0),
    (0.0208, 0.0208),
    (0.0, 0.0208),
    (0.0, 0.0)
]

inner_loop = [
    (0.0013, 0.0013),
    (0.0195, 0.0013),
    (0.0195, 0.0195),
    (0.0013, 0.0195),
    (0.0013, 0.0013)
]

# Create the sketch
r = r.polyline(outer_loop).close().polyline(inner_loop).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer rectangle
r = r.box(0.0208, 0.0208, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# Define the inner rectangle
inner_rectangle = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.0188, 0.0188, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False)).translate((0.002, 0.002, 0))

# Cut the inner rectangle from the outer rectangle
r = r.cut(inner_rectangle)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
